body: What is the role of metformin in type 2 diabetes?

documents.title: Metformin and diabetes
documents.text: Metformin is commonly used as a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes. It reduces hepatic glucose production and can improve insulin sensitivity.

documents.title: Diabetes medicines
documents.text: Lifestyle intervention is important in diabetes care. Some medicines can cause hypoglycemia, so treatment should be individualized.

documents.title: Metformin safety
documents.text: Metformin is associated with gastrointestinal adverse effects. Kidney function should be considered when prescribing it.

snippets.text: Metformin is commonly used as a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes.
It reduces hepatic glucose production and can improve insulin sensitivity.

ideal_answer: Metformin is commonly used as a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes because it reduces hepatic glucose production and can improve insulin sensitivity.

body: Does vaccination reduce severe influenza outcomes?

documents.title: Influenza vaccination
documents.text: Influenza vaccination reduces the risk of severe influenza outcomes in many populations. Effectiveness varies by season and strain.

documents.title: Influenza symptoms
documents.text: Influenza can cause fever, cough, and fatigue. Supportive care may be used for uncomplicated illness.

snippets.text: Influenza vaccination reduces the risk of severe influenza outcomes in many populations.

ideal_answer: Yes, vaccination reduces the risk of severe influenza outcomes, although effectiveness varies by season and strain.

body: Which vitamin is associated with scurvy prevention?

documents.title: Vitamin C
documents.text: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy. Adequate vitamin C intake prevents scurvy.

documents.title: Vitamin D
documents.text: Vitamin D supports calcium homeostasis and bone health.

snippets.text: Adequate vitamin C intake prevents scurvy.

ideal_answer: Vitamin C is associated with prevention of scurvy.

body: What is the main function of hemoglobin?

documents.title: Hemoglobin
documents.text: Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that transports oxygen from the lungs to tissues.

documents.title: Platelets
documents.text: Platelets participate in blood clotting and wound repair.

snippets.text: Hemoglobin transports oxygen from the lungs to tissues.

ideal_answer: Hemoglobin transports oxygen from the lungs to tissues.

documents.title: Pancreas
documents.text: The pancreas produces insulin in beta cells located in the islets of Langerhans.

documents.title: Liver
documents.text: The liver stores glycogen and performs many metabolic functions.

snippets.text: The pancreas produces insulin in beta cells.

ideal_answer: The pancreas produces insulin in beta cells.

body: Is anemia associated with reduced hemoglobin?

documents.title: Anemia
documents.text: Anemia is a condition in which the blood has a reduced capacity to carry oxygen, often because hemoglobin is reduced.

documents.title: White blood cells
documents.text: White blood cells help protect the body against infection.

snippets.text: Anemia is often associated with reduced hemoglobin.

ideal_answer: Yes. Anemia is often associated with reduced hemoglobin and reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.
